diagrams.title: Turn Search Demand into Owned Publishing Assets
diagrams.subtitle: Five operating stages connect useful pages to publisher revenue.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The operating sequence covers multi-site search publishing, selective programmatic production, and GEO citation tracking. Stage numbers express sequence, not revenue forecasts. The canonical time to first deal is 3–12 months.
diagrams.caption: Automate technical audits, refresh queues, and revenue reporting; retain human responsibility for evidence, rights, and editorial quality.

stages.label: Map demand
stages.detail: Combine Google Search Console, Ahrefs, and direct SERP inspection to map intent, competing formats, audience needs, and plausible advertising or affiliate demand.

stages.label: Design assets
stages.value: Stage 2: establish evidence and page architecture
stages.detail: Specify original research, licensed media, internal links, and differentiated page templates. Reject programmatic variants that add no substantive user value.

stages.label: Publish and verify
stages.detail: Use Screaming Frog and Search Console to inspect status codes, canonicals, rendering, and indexability. Editors verify claims, contributor rights, and commercial disclosures.

stages.label: Monetize earned attention
stages.detail: Record advertising earnings, approved affiliate commissions, and delivered sponsorship revenue. Exclude referred merchant sales, pending commissions, and undelivered sponsor commitments.

stages.label: Refresh and package
stages.value: Stage 5: reinvest using auditable asset records
stages.detail: Queue decaying pages in Airtable; reconcile revenue in BigQuery and Looker Studio. Log sampled GEO citations separately from referrals and maintain transfer-ready rights records.

diagrams.title: Measure One Cohort through Payable Affiliate Outcomes
diagrams.subtitle: 100,000 eligible organic sessions narrow to 530 payable sessions.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative cohort, not observed performance or an annual projection. Every downstream count is a subset of the original 100,000 sessions, counted once per stage. Use permitted attribution records and a stated 60-day reconciliation window. Assume exactly one $20 approved commission per payable session.
diagrams.caption: The cohort earns $10,600 in affiliate revenue: 530 multiplied by $20. Merchant order value is excluded. Advertising and sponsorship earnings are outside this conversion funnel.

stages.label: Organic entry sessions
stages.detail: Freeze eligible organic landing sessions for the cohort period. Exclude internal traffic and bot traffic; document measurement exclusions instead of treating them as conversions.

stages.label: Commercial-content readers
stages.detail: Count sessions reaching at least one relevant comparison or product-selection page. Multiple page views within the same session do not enlarge this stage.

stages.label: Affiliate outbound sessions
stages.detail: Count sessions with at least one disclosed affiliate outbound event. Preserve campaign and content identifiers without transmitting unnecessary personal information.

stages.label: Attributed purchase sessions
stages.detail: Match merchant-reported purchase events back to eligible outbound sessions. Deduplicate purchases within each session and retain pending status during returns review.

stages.label: Payable purchase sessions
stages.detail: Remove 70 sessions whose purchases were reversed or disallowed. Final conversion is 0.53% of the original cohort; reconcile $10,600 to approved commission statements.

diagrams.title: Reconcile $490,000 Gross to $159,250 Owner Net
diagrams.subtitle: Four illustrative cost deductions produce the canonical 32.5% margin.
diagrams.assumptions_note: First and last bars are totals; the four intervening bars are negative deductions. Revenue and owner net are canonical; cost category allocations are illustrative. Annual costs total $330,750, or $27,562.50 monthly. The supplied $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex range cannot be an all-in ceiling for this Base case: implied annual costs exceed its $240,000 upper annual equivalent by $90,750. Resolve that scope difference before budgeting.
diagrams.caption: $490,000 minus $156,000 minus $84,000 minus $42,000 minus $48,750 equals $159,250; $159,250 divided by $490,000 equals 32.5%. Referred merchant sales never enter publisher gross revenue.

stages.label: Publisher gross revenue
stages.detail: Illustrative rail allocation is $218,000 advertising, $212,000 approved affiliate commissions, and $60,000 delivered sponsorship revenue; the three components reconcile.

stages.label: Full-time labor
stages.detail: Allocate $156,000 to the single full-time seat in the 1 FT + 3 C core pod. Treat this as a modeled loaded labor budget, not a salary survey finding or a separate owner distribution.

stages.label: Contracted production
stages.detail: The core pod includes three fractional contractor seats, not four. The unchanged $84,000 production envelope covers their purchased capacity and any external vendor/trade sub-crews charged to direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through. External crews are not internal pod headcount; do not add their costs again outside this deduction.

stages.label: Publishing infrastructure
stages.detail: Budget hosting, security maintenance, audit tools, analytics, licensed datasets, and production software. Separate one-time setup purchases from recurring costs to prevent duplication.

stages.label: Commercial and administrative costs
stages.detail: Allocate $24,000 to commercial development, $12,000 to bookkeeping and contract administration, and $12,750 to insurance, banking, and other incurred operating expenses.

stages.label: Annual owner net profit
stages.detail: Preserve the canonical Base result. Conservative revenue of $80,000 at 20% yields $16,000; Scaled revenue of $900,000 at 45% yields $405,000.

diagrams.title: Compare Sub-Niches on Publisher Revenue per 1,000 Sessions
diagrams.subtitle: Equal traffic allocations produce a $49 blended publisher yield.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Illustrative yields, not market benchmarks. Allocate 2,000,000 annual sessions to each of five sub-niches: 10,000,000 sessions total. All yield components are USD of operator revenue per 1,000 sessions, after affiliate reversals. Equal traffic weighting produces $49 blended yield and $490,000 annual Base revenue.
diagrams.caption: Across the five equal-traffic segments, advertising contributes $218,000, affiliate commissions $212,000, and sponsorships $60,000. Yield comparisons require consistent session definitions and periods.

stages.label: Home workshop references
stages.detail: $18 advertising plus $10 affiliate commissions plus $2 sponsorship equals $30. At 2,000,000 annual sessions, publisher revenue is $60,000; original photos reduce rights risk.

stages.label: Outdoor equipment guides
stages.detail: $20 advertising plus $15 affiliate commissions plus $5 sponsorship equals $40. At 2,000,000 annual sessions, publisher revenue is $80,000; monitor seasonal traffic concentration.

stages.label: Creative software tutorials
stages.detail: $22 advertising plus $23 affiliate commissions plus $5 sponsorship equals $50. At 2,000,000 annual sessions, publisher revenue is $100,000; refresh screenshots after interface changes.

stages.label: Small-business workflow guides
stages.detail: $24 advertising plus $28 affiliate commissions plus $8 sponsorship equals $60. At 2,000,000 annual sessions, publisher revenue is $120,000; verify affiliate attribution windows.

stages.label: Specialist software comparisons
stages.detail: $25 advertising plus $30 affiliate commissions plus $10 sponsorship equals $65. At 2,000,000 annual sessions, publisher revenue is $130,000; monitor partner concentration and reversals.

diagrams.title: Resolve Rights, Claims, Privacy, and Distribution before Release
diagrams.subtitle: Each affirmative answer advances; each negative answer triggers repair.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four sequential yes-or-no checks. A failed check sends the affected page, tracking feature, or outreach campaign to the named corrective action before reassessment. Statutory duties depend on the activity and applicable jurisdiction; search platform policies are separate contractual and distribution risks.
diagrams.caption: Record evidence, the responsible owner, and the corrective action. Do not treat an automated SEO score as proof of copyright permission, truthful advertising, or lawful data handling.

stages.label: Rights established?
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: replace or document permission
stages.detail: Editor checks text, images, datasets, and contributor agreements against 17 U.S.C. 106, 107, and 204. Fair use requires specific analysis; attribution alone does not grant reproduction rights.

stages.label: Commercial claims supportable?
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: correct claims and disclosures
stages.detail: Commercial lead checks evidence under 15 U.S.C. 45 and material connections under 16 CFR 255.5. Place clear disclosures with endorsements; do not bury paid relationships in a distant policy page.

stages.label: Data handling scoped?
stages.value: Yes: advance; no: disable affected collection
stages.detail: Technical lead maps identifiers, recipients, retention, and applicable rights. Assess Cal. Civ. Code 1798.100, 1798.120, and 1798.140 applicability; assess COPPA under 15 U.S.C. 6502 and 16 CFR 312 for child-directed services or relevant actual knowledge.

stages.label: Distribution method acceptable?
stages.value: Yes: release; no: revise outreach or templates
stages.detail: Operator checks commercial email against 15 U.S.C. 7704, including accurate headers and functioning opt-out. Separately inspect Google spam policies for scaled content abuse, link spam, and site reputation abuse.

diagrams.title: Operate Four Core Seats; Add Two Only in the Scaled Model
diagrams.subtitle: Conservative and Base: 1 FT + 3 C. Scaled: 2 FT + 4 C.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Six entries depict four core seats and two Scaled-only expansion seats. A numeric value of 1 marks a person included in the core pod; 0 marks an expansion seat excluded from core headcount, not an unstaffed role once scaled. The core is 1 FT + 3 C (4 people); adding 1 FT + 1 C produces 2 FT + 4 C (6 people). Contractor seats are fractional service relationships, not full-time equivalents. External vendor/trade sub-crews are direct subcontractor/COGS pass-through, not internal pod seats. FYMC 2.0 score: 89/100; rank #07 of 29; tier: Elite Small-Team Cash Machine.
diagrams.caption: The four-person core supports the canonical $80,000 Conservative and $490,000 Base scenarios; the six-person configuration belongs to the $900,000 Scaled scenario. Add the full-time partnerships lead and contracted production specialist only when funded workload justifies expansion. Resize paid capacity for Conservative revenue; scenario revenue alone does not establish workload capacity.

stages.label: Portfolio operator
stages.value: Core seat 1: full-time portfolio and commercial ownership
stages.detail: Own topic allocation, site-level profit reporting, partner concentration, and capital deployment. Reconcile advertising, payable affiliate commissions, and delivered sponsorships. Maintain the rights register and transaction-ready records; retain commercial responsibility until the expansion lead joins.

stages.label: Managing editor
stages.detail: Own evidence standards, contributor briefs, publishing cadence, and refresh priorities within contracted capacity. Review commercial claims, contributor rights, and disclosure placement; prevent duplicative programmatic page expansion.

stages.label: Technical SEO engineer
stages.detail: Maintain crawl monitoring, template tests, structured data, analytics connectors, and deployment checks. Route indexing regressions to a tracked repair queue instead of mass resubmission; support the operator's revenue reporting.

stages.label: Subject and production specialist
stages.value: Core seat 4: contracted research, writing, and CMS production
stages.detail: Produce original explanations, testing records, and attributable expert contributions. Supply source packets and documented media rights, format accessible pages, and verify internal links. Scope combined research and production work to purchased capacity rather than assuming multiple full-time roles.

stages.label: Growth partnerships lead
stages.value: Scaled-only seat 5: additional full-time commercial owner
stages.detail: Add one FT seat in the Scaled configuration to diversify sponsorships and manage partner renewals. Protect editorial independence and document placement obligations before recognizing sponsor revenue; this seat is outside the core pod.

stages.label: Production specialist
stages.value: Scaled-only seat 6: additional contracted production capacity
stages.detail: Add one C seat in the Scaled configuration for licensed visuals, accessible CMS formatting, and publication checks. Relieve the core subject specialist's production workload only after measuring editorial review capacity and the refresh backlog; this seat is outside the core pod.

diagrams.title: Allocate a $35,000 Reference Startup Plan across Four Buckets
diagrams.subtitle: Lean $10,000, reference $35,000, and expanded $60,000 USD launch plans.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Numeric values depict the $35,000 central/reference startup budget within the canonical $10,000–$60,000 USD range. Each bucket also specifies lean and expanded allocations; all three plans use 40%, 30%, 20%, and 10% shares and sum exactly to $10,000, $35,000, and $60,000 respectively. These are illustrative cash allocations, not accounting capitalization instructions or additional annual costs. Expanded startup funding does not automatically activate the Scaled pod.
diagrams.caption: Lean: $4,000 + $3,000 + $2,000 + $1,000 = $10,000. Reference: $14,000 + $10,500 + $7,000 + $3,500 = $35,000. Expanded: $24,000 + $18,000 + $12,000 + $6,000 = $60,000. Budget continuing funding separately for the canonical 3–12 months to first deal and $2,500–$14,000 USD monthly opex range; startup capital alone does not guarantee sufficient runway.

stages.label: Original content and evidence
stages.detail: Allocate $4,000 of the $10,000 lean plan, $14,000 of the $35,000 reference plan, or $24,000 of the $60,000 expanded plan. Fund original testing, commissioned writing, editing, and documented media licenses.

stages.label: Technical publishing foundation
stages.detail: Allocate $3,000 of the $10,000 lean plan, $10,500 of the $35,000 reference plan, or $18,000 of the $60,000 expanded plan. Fund templates, hosting setup, backups, access controls, and initial crawl remediation.

stages.label: Measurement and commercial setup
stages.detail: Allocate $2,000 of the $10,000 lean plan, $7,000 of the $35,000 reference plan, or $12,000 of the $60,000 expanded plan. Fund attribution setup, reporting connectors, partner materials, and contributor agreement preparation.

stages.label: Unspent working reserve
stages.detail: Allocate $1,000 of the $10,000 lean plan, $3,500 of the $35,000 reference plan, or $6,000 of the $60,000 expanded plan. The reference reserve covers 1.4 months at $2,500 monthly opex or 0.25 months at $14,000. Reserve cash is not an incurred expense; avoid counting the same funded activity again as an additional cash need.

diagrams.title: Use the First 30 Days to Establish a Measurable Publishing System
diagrams.subtitle: Ship an evidence-backed pilot, not a promised first-month revenue result.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Four weekly milestones span Days 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, and 22–30. Numeric values are milestone end days. Deliverable counts are sprint planning assumptions for the four-person core pod (1 FT + 3 C), not traffic forecasts. First-deal timing remains the canonical 3–12 months.
diagrams.caption: Finish with a tested pilot, documented rights, functioning revenue definitions, and a funded next sprint. Ranking losses, slow audience growth, and revenue concentration remain explicit risks.

stages.label: Days 1–7
stages.value: Select one site and one evidence-backed cluster
stages.detail: Operator and editor map 30 queries, review ten competing pages, and select one initial site. Record expected revenue rails, rights requirements, and a twelve-month cash plan.

stages.label: Days 8–14
stages.value: Test two templates and commission ten briefs
stages.detail: Technical contractor validates canonicals, indexing controls, mobile rendering, and analytics events. Editor commissions ten distinct briefs and completes the four publication checks.

stages.label: Days 15–21
stages.value: Publish ten reviewed pages with traceable evidence
stages.detail: Release the pilot after editorial and technical review. Connect internal links, submit the sitemap, and sample GEO citations across twenty fixed prompts while recording engine, date, wording, and cited destination.

stages.label: Days 22–30
stages.value: Audit the pilot and fund the next sprint
stages.detail: Review crawl results, measured impressions, referral events, and production hours. Test revenue reconciliation with clearly labeled synthetic records; rank refresh work and record cash needs without counting pending deals as revenue.
